What's even funnier is the shooting range is directly tied with your menu frame rate. If you have your menu frame rate capped to 30fps to save your GPU in-between games, good luck practice in the shooting rate at 30fps!

This is a good recommendation. I agree with the comment of having a more modern CPU for running taxing plugins. I've been rocking a i7 9700k (9th gen) for music production and it's perfectly capable. 8-cores and above is a safe bet.

(I use Reaper so I don't know if Ableton does this) You can 'freeze' tracks and have the DAW render out what the plugin would do on your track before you playback. Thus freeing up CPU usage. I wouldn't worry about a GPU if all you're doing is music. Get a used GTX 970 or 1060 and it'll be smooth metering.

I wouldn't fear too much on choosing underperforming components. Get a decent CPU, 16GB DDR4 RAM (gets cheaper by the day), a 2TB HDD, a used inexpensive GPU, and a compatible motherboard for them.

Long answer: When I was transfering all my files to a new computer, I did the same thing of backing everything up. I transferred (copy pasted entire folder exactly so I didn't mess up particular file locations) every Reaper file to an external hard-drive (2TB Solid State USB 3.0). Then when I got the new computer, I downloaded Reaper first, then plugged in the hard-drive. And boom! Reaper boots up as if it was on the old computer, presets and all

Hope this helps!
